Hi Monica — great to continue the conversation. High level first, then a recommended route based on deal size and compliance constraints.

TL;DR recommendations
- Fast pilot (<= $50k): marketplace listing (public or private offer) is the fastest path — reduced procurement friction and immediate invoicing via cloud provider.
- Expansion with co-sell intent: use a private offer on the marketplace (we can co-sell and nominate) so you get cloud procurement speed with co-sell alignment.
- Enterprise / custom legal/SOC2/data residency needs: direct purchase under Redwood MSA + PO (slower; full contractual control).

Key differences (short):
- Seller-of-record & invoices: marketplace purchases are typically billed by the cloud provider or by Redwood through the marketplace depending on the provider and the offer type (public listing vs private offer). For AWS Marketplace private offers, Redwood remains seller-of-record but the invoice flows are handled in the marketplace billing; for Azure, it can be partner-billed or Microsoft-billed depending on listing type. That affects your accounting mapping and who sends the invoice.
- Co-sell credits: co-sell nomination and credit recognition are possible with private offers but timing/eligibility varies by cloud and sometimes require registration at purchase time. Direct contracts give more immediate attribution for Redwood-sourced deals if the cloud partner program requires seller nomination through the marketplace path — we can walk through the exact nomination steps.
- Contractual terms & data residency: direct MSA gives the most control (SLA, indemnities, data retention). Marketplace offers often reference provider terms; private offers allow attachment of custom terms in many cases but can be slower to set up if legal needs carveouts.

I'll loop in Aditya and Laura with a one-pager and a pragmatic timeline for each route. If you can confirm target cloud(s) for the pilot and whether the pilot will process PHI, that will determine recommendations on data handling and whether we need a BAA.

- Aditya: provide private-offer timing and co-sell steps (tomorrow)

Monica — adding a couple pragmatic notes and an attached one-pager that summarizes mechanics per cloud.

Attached: Redwood_Marketplace_vs_Direct_Pricing_OnePager.pdf

Practical notes by cloud:
- AWS: For a quick pilot, AWS Marketplace (public listing or private offer) is quickest. Private Offer gives you standard PO flow and we can set price/term. Seller-of-record typically remains Redwood for private offers; invoice reconciliation is via AWS billing. Co-sell: nomination at purchase or through the AWS co-sell desk — recognition can lag 30–90 days depending on AWS processing.
- Azure: Azure Marketplace private offers let you maintain partner billing and co-sell paths; public offers may route billing through Microsoft. Co-sell crediting requires an Azure Marketplace listing and a seller nomination; timing similar to AWS.
- GCP: GCP Marketplace commonly uses partner billing for private offers; co-sell/partner referral programs exist, but GCP tends to require a sponsored procurement route for co-sell attribution.

Trade-offs (very short):
- Time to PO: marketplace < private offer setup < direct MSA negotiation
- Control over terms: direct MSA > private offer > public marketplace
- Co-sell attribution: private offer (marketplace) gives the best balance of speed + co-sell eligibility

Recommended timelines (ballpark):
- Marketplace public (simple listing): 2–5 business days to purchase if you already have an account and approval flow
- Marketplace private offer setup: 3–10 business days to configure pricing and PO reconciliation
- Direct MSA + PO: 2–6 weeks (legal reviews can extend this)

If you want we can start a private-offer setup for AWS for the pilot and simultaneously circulate the MSA so you have an executed agreement if you expand.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales Operations
